Subject: Renewal: Support Ladder & Latency Guardrails

Hi Alyssa,

Our accounts team noticed your contract renewal window opens in ~45 days. Given the latency issues you flagged in Q3 and the planned expansion for your personalization pipeline, I wanted to propose an optional premium support + latency guardrails package to include with the renewal:

- Premium SLA: 99.95% availability for the inference control plane, with defined incident response times (P1 initial response: 30 min).
- Latency SLOs: target p95 < 120ms, p99 < 350ms for the reserved capacity profile; tail guarantees with fallbacks to compatible model variants.
- Dedicated reserved capacity: configurable burst pool for scheduled campaigns and unplanned spikes.
- Onboarding runbook, 60-day ramp with weekly checkpoints, and a playbook for failover to hosted variants.

Estimated commercial delta: we expect a ~20% committed spend uplift vs your current committed tier for the above (I attached a pricing sketch). I also attached Q3 latency metrics we collected (latency_metrics_q3.csv) and proposal draft (redwood_proposal_v3.pdf).

Questions for you:
1) Is Acme interested in a 12-mo premium SLA add-on or would you prefer a 6-mo pilot (with conditional SLA rollout)?
2) What is your expected steady-state QPS during peak personalization windows (rough ballpark is fine)?
3) Who from procurement should we loop in to expedite contract and SOW?

If useful I can put Marcus on a short call tomorrow to walk the technical constraints and Vanessa to cover onboarding timelines.

Thanks,
Chloe Martin
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0164

Chloe — thanks for the quick outreach and for the attachments. A few quick data points / asks from our side:

- We hit a sharp latency tail event during the holiday promo cadence in Sept (p99 spikes to ~900ms for ~30 minutes). That’s the principal driver for considering a premium SLA.
- We're open to a 6-month pilot with SLA ramp if you can commit to an explicit burst-capacity playbook and clear RTO for P1 incidents.
- We need a clearer picture on the commercial math — can you convert the ~20% uplift into concrete $/month for our current commit? Also highlight any licensing / per-token exceptions.

Procurement: Kenji is on copy — Kenji, please advise preferred contracting cadence and if Acme will require PO-first or DocuSign.

Can we do a working session Thursday 11/9 10:00–10:45 PT for Marcus to walk through the reserve/burst sizing and for Vanessa to outline onboarding?

Best,

Alyssa — thanks for the context. Quick technical clarifications and a concrete cost stub to help procurement: 

Technical:
- Reserved capacity model: we carve a dedicated GPU pool for your model family with autoscale headroom and a burst pool that shields the reserved path for short spikes. That burst pool is enforced with guardrails to avoid noisy-neighbor amplification.
- Expected latency (based on your Q3 trace and our test profile): p95 ~ 90–110ms, p99 ~ 280–360ms on reserved capacity for your current model. The p99 tail you saw in Sept correlates with saturated KV cache and long-running batched requests; mitigation: KV-prefetch + stricter batching thresholds during high-traffic windows.
- SLA/penalties: the premium SLA includes credits for missed availability thresholds and a commitment to a 30-min P1 response and a 4-hour P1 mitigation window.

Commercial stub (illustrative):
- Current committed monthly spend: $135,000
- Premium SLA + reserved capacity uplift (baseline): +20% => ~$162,000 / month
- Optional burst-capacity buffer (on-demand, metered): +$6–12k in months with heavy campaigns
- DocuSign SOW to reflect an initial 6-month pilot with opt-in to 12-mo full term after successful ramp.

Operational timelines:
- Provisioning reserved capacity: 7–10 business days after SOW + payment/PO.
- Onboarding & playbook delivery: kickoff + 4 weeks for runbook and dry-run, then 30–60 days of ramp.

I can prepare a short technical appendix to accompany the commercial SOW if that would help Kenji. Confirm peak QPS estimate and I’ll produce a tailored sizing doc.

—Marcus

Alyssa / team — looping in a quick onboarding plan so expectations are aligned if you choose the 6-mo pilot -> 12-mo conversion path: 

Week 0: Paperwork & provisioning (PO or DocuSign)
Week 1–2: Kickoff, runbook review, escalation contact mapping, on-call rotation alignment
Week 3–6: Dry-run traffic tests, KV warm-up, and failover rehearsals; weekly checkpoints
Week 7–12: Live ramp; measure against SLOs and refine batching thresholds

Deliverables we’ll provide: runbook, playbook for burst events, documented rollback steps, and a shared incident channel for the pilot.

Ask from Acme: please share target campaign windows (dates/times) and an internal point-of-contact for SRE during the dry-run so we can schedule the rehearsals without surprises.

If Kenji can confirm procurement preference (PO-first vs DocuSign), Chloe and I will route the final SOW accordingly and attach the DocuSign link.

Chloe / Alyssa — thanks for the details and timeline. Acme is prepared to proceed with the 12-month premium SLA but we'd like to start with a 6-month pilot clause baked into the SOW: the first 6 months with an observed SLO acceptance checklist, automatically continuing to 12 months if metrics are met. Two requests from procurement before we sign:

1) A clear $/month number to replace the “~20% uplift” line item so our finance team can approve; please provide a monthly invoice schedule and any up-front fees.
2) A first-month credit of $15,000 if the pilot fails to meet the agreed p99 guardrail for any two distinct incidents during the pilot window.

We prefer DocuSign routing; I've attached a draft PO (acme_po_draft.pdf) for Redwood to reference. Please send the final SOW + DocuSign link and an updated pricing table and we will route for signature this week.
